about.text: Leyden, from Dutch: Leidse kaas, is a semi-hard, cumin and caraway seed flavoured cheese made in the Netherlands from cow's milk. It is made both in factories and on farms, historically in the Leiden area.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.
cumin and caraway; partly skimmed; PDO (1997) is for farmhouse Boeren-Leidse met sleutels; article gives no ripening time

facts.v: Historically a by-product of butter-making, from part-skimmed milk, so lower in fat than Gouda
Young cheese has a red rind, coloured with annatto
